state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap`, `Core\Ldap\Filter`, `Core\Ldap\Dn`, `Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad`, `Core\Ldap\Change`, `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType`, `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and `Core\Ldap\Connection::compare` owe nothing.

**What is still owed:** `Core\Ldap\Connection::setPassword` and `changePassword` owe `about.md`, three examples, one attack and one bench each; their tests are credited now (`covers:` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs` and `tests/conformance/core/ldap-set-password.nvst`). `Core\Ldap\Entry::isDeleted` owes `about.md`, three examples, one attack and one bench. `Core\Ldap\Entries` (`references`, `total`) and `Core\Ldap\Changes::cookie` owe everything, and `total` and `cookie` also owe a Rust test with a `covers:` marker.

**The proof trees are granted `[ldap.corp]` by directory** in the root `nvs.toml`, under each of the three trees, for `Ldap-Entry`, `Ldap-Ad-GroupType`, `Ldap-Ad-AccountFlags` and `Ldap-Connection`. A new directory such as `Ldap-Entries` needs its own `[[app]] root` grant in all three trees, and an `[[app]] root` that names a missing directory fails every program in the repository with `E0605`. Check a draft with `bun nv proofs --run --id '<feature>' --show`: it takes **one** `--id`. `--bless` takes files, never a directory. `--record-perf` fails its calibration while `bun nv verify` runs, so run the two one after the other, and start `--record-perf` in the background.

**`[ldap.corp]` binds as the read-only `Reader`**, so it cannot run `setPassword` or `changePassword`. The seed (`tests/db/compose.yaml:416`) has `Administrator` with `Novis-test-1` and the users with `Novis-user-1`, and the domain keeps a password history of 24. The safe shape for a write example is a second block in the root `nvs.toml`, granted only to the `Ldap-Connection` password directories, that binds as `Administrator`, and a program that adds its own user under `OU=Company`, sets or changes that user's password and deletes the user again, the way `tests/conformance/core/ldap-set-password.nvst` does with `CN=Staff`. Name the block for the directory it reaches and its task (for example `[ldap.corp-accounts]`), never for a judgement. The `[ldap.corp]` grant on `docs/examples/core/Ldap-Connection` covers all of that directory, so the password programs need the new block added to the same three `[[app]]` entries.

**Seeded facts a proof can print:** people are `CN=Anna Berg`, `CN=Ben Kohl`, `CN=Carla Diaz` and `CN=Dora Lind` under `OU=Company`; `department` is `Sales` for Anna and Carla and `Warehouse` for Ben and Dora; only Anna has a `title` and is in `Managers`. RIDs follow the seed order (`Reader` 1103, `Employees` 1104, `Managers` 1105, `Newsletter` 1106, `anna.berg` 1107), `Administrator` is 500. `userAccountControl` is 512 for `anna.berg` and `carla.diaz`, 514 for `dora.lind` and 66048 for `ben.kohl` and `Reader`. GUIDs, SIDs and timestamps differ per boot.

**`Reader` cannot read any attribute of a deleted object**, so `isDeleted()` is `false` on everything it can find, and the seed deletes nothing.
